codeReview.summary: The retry helper changes in `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` largely match the requested 5xx/429 backoff policy, but the feature does not wire that behavior into the frontend's real request paths and never connects the new retry-state hook to any rendered UI. As shipped, transient failures for the app's existing authenticated API calls still fail immediately, and the hook update also narrows `RequestInit` compatibility in a shared helper.

issues.description: Updating the returned `authFetch` callback does not make the application's authenticated requests retry in practice. `ProtectedLayoutShell` only invokes `useAuthenticatedFetch()` for its side effect (`frontend/src/components/layout/ProtectedLayoutShell.tsx:106`) and ignores the returned callback, while real request sites still call `apiFetch(...)` directly (`frontend/src/features/workflows/hooks/useWorkflowsPage.ts:323`, `frontend/src/features/profiles/hooks/useProfilesPage.ts:181`, `frontend/src/components/shared/useLogsState.ts:259`, etc.). Because those flows never reach `authFetch`, the feature does not deliver retry/backoff for the frontend's existing authenticated API traffic.

The new retry-state hook is dead code. Repository search only finds `useApiCall` in its own definition file, so no component actually renders `state.isLoading`, `state.isRetrying`, or `state.retryAttempt` during backoff. That leaves the feature without an implementation of the requirement that the frontend show loading/retry state during retries instead of surfacing only the eventual error.

`authFetch` used to forward arbitrary `RequestInit` into `fetch`. The new implementation assumes the body is a JSON string (`JSON.parse(body as string)`) and drops the rest of `RequestInit` such as `headers`, `signal`, `credentials`, and other fetch options. Any future caller passing `FormData`, plain text, already-parsed objects, or custom headers would break or silently lose options before the network request is sent.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared project knowledge does not clearly document that `useAuthenticatedFetch` is primarily a token-registration side-effect hook while most real frontend API requests go through `apiFetch` and the module-level `tokenGetter` directly. That gap makes it easy to assume changing the hook's returned callback changes all authenticated request behavior.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `frontend/src/components/layout/ProtectedLayoutShell.tsx:106` calls `useAuthenticatedFetch()` and ignores the return value, `frontend/src/lib/api.ts:4-40` shows `apiFetch` reads the module-level `tokenGetter`, and grep across `docs/` / `.factory/library/` finds no explanatory note about that relationship beyond file listings. The worker transcript explicitly concluded that updating `useAuthenticatedFetch` would make 'all auth requests go through retry wrapper', which is not how the codebase actually works.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `refactor-worker`'s testing procedure does not account for frontend-only changes in this repo where no frontend test harness exists, yet handoffs can still report the procedure as fully followed with no deviation recorded.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/skills/refactor-worker/SKILL.md` Step 3 says new functionality should get failing tests first, `AGENTS.md` says 'No frontend tests — out of scope', and this handoff reports `tests.added: []` plus `skillFeedback.followedProcedure: true`. That mismatch suggests the skill should explicitly describe how to handle frontend behavior changes when only build/lint validation is available.

summary: Reviewed the feature metadata, handoff, transcript skeleton, skill file, and commit `81097f3cef29602c22d2c64e7f95eeca6b76887e`. The review fails because the new retry logic is not connected to the frontend's real authenticated request paths and the new retry-state hook is unused, so the requested runtime retry behavior and UI retry-state behavior are not actually delivered.
